To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) pixel level out of distribution detection is a difficult task and the performance of state of the art image level out of distribution methods is significantly worse when applied to this task; 2) the performance of the compared methods is not correlated with performance on image classification, and; 3) a new evaluation metric is proposed that is more appropriate for the pixel level out of distributions detection task.
(i) The performance ranking of state-of-the-art image-level OOD methods does not transfer when adapting the methods to the new task.
the performance of OOD detection for semantic segmentation is worse than that for image classification, and that the performance ranking for the two tasks is not transferable.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How can the detection of out of the distribution pixels be evaluated? How can the detection methods be adapted to the new task? How well do the detection methods work in practice?
the question of whether pixel-level out of distribution detection can be used to localise the objects that cause the image to be considered out of distribution.
the task of detecting out-of-distribution pixels for semantic segmentation and the efficacy of pixel-level out of distribution detection methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pixel-level out of distribution detection task is significantly more difficult than the image-level task.
there is no effective method of pixel-level out of distribution detection.
there are no methods that are effective at pixel-level out of distribution detection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the task of detecting out-of-distribution images is significantly easier than the task of detecting pixels out-of-distribution.
pixel-level OOD detection is a challenging task and the performance is not yet at an acceptable level.
the task of pixel-level OOD detection is significantly harder than the image-level task, but the adapted methods still provide some improvement over a baseline.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pixel-level OOD detection is a challenging task that requires further investigation.
the current methods for detecting out distribution pixels are not suitable for the semantic segmentation task.
the current methods are not suitable for detecting out of distributions pixels.
